transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well, I guess mostly I'm just having trouble sleeping lately. It's gotten pretty unreliable. Even when I go to bed exhausted, I just... lie there. I end up replaying work stuff, like sales forecasts or issues with my team. And then I usually wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and... I just can't get my brain to power down again after that.
Are these sleep issues affecting your daily life or work in any way?

Um... yeah, I suppose it is. It's... well, at work, I've been second-guessing my decisions a lot lately. It makes the pipeline reviews with my team pretty tense. And... I don't know, by the time I get home, I'm just so drained. I end up being kind of reactive with my husband... just not really fully present with him, I guess.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things, outside of just work?

Um... I guess so. It's... mostly work, I think. But... yeah, it spills over. Most days it's just... my mind jumps around a lot. Like, I'll be thinking about if we're going to hit the launch numbers, and then suddenly I'm worrying if someone on my team is going to quit. And then... I don't know, it just moves on to the mortgage, or a client renewal. It just feels like... like any small delay is going to turn into some major disaster.
Is there any part of your life where you feel you don't worry excessively?
Um... I don't know. I guess... not really. It just sort of feels like it's always there, in the background.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
Um... no. I don't think so. Not like that.
Have you ever felt a sudden, intense fear or discomfort that came on very quickly?
Um... no. Like I just said... not really. I haven't felt anything like that.
Do you think your sleep problems started before or after you began worrying excessively about work and other things?
Um... I'm not really sure. It's hard to tell... they just sort of blend together, I guess. I haven't really thought about which one came first.
Are there more days than not where you feel like you're worrying excessively about things?

Yeah, I guess so. Most days, probably. I just... my mind kind of jumps around a lot. Like, I'll be thinking about whether we'll hit our launch numbers at work, and then suddenly I'm worrying about if someone on my team is going to quit. And then it's the mortgage, or a client renewal... it just feels like any little delay could turn into some huge problem. It's just... a lot of days are like that.
Do you feel like your worrying is causing you a lot of distress?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. It's... it's starting to affect things. Like at work, I spend so much time second-guessing my decisions that... well, the pipeline reviews just get pretty tense. And then... I guess by the time I get home, I'm just really drained. I end up being kind of reactive... and I'm not really fully present with my husband. So... yeah, I guess it is.
Is your difficulty sleeping present on nights when you aren't worrying about work or other things?
Um... I'm not really sure. I don't really keep track of that.
Do you have trouble sleeping even on nights when you aren't worried about anything in particular?
Um... I think that's kind of what you just asked, right? I... I really don't know. It's hard to tell if there's ever a night where my mind is just completely blank. So... yeah, I'm not sure.
Do you ever have nights where you aren't worried about anything and still have trouble sleeping?
I... I feel like we're going in circles. I don't know how else to answer that. I just... I don't really have nights where I'm not worrying about *something*.
Do you think your sleep problems would improve if you weren't worrying about work and other things?
I mean... maybe? I guess it makes sense that it would help, but... I don't really know for sure. I haven't really experienced that, so it's hard to say.
Is your excessive worrying usually about a specific area of your life, like work, or is it more about a wide range of everyday things?

Um... I guess it's a bit of everything. It just... jumps around. Like, I'll be worrying about whether we'll hit our launch numbers at work, or... if someone on my team is about to quit. But then it's also... the mortgage, or a client renewal. It just feels like... any small delay could turn into something major. So... yeah, it's not really just one thing.
Do you think your worrying would decrease if your sleep improved?
I... I really don't know. Um... I haven't slept well in so long that... I can't really say. I just don't know if it would change anything.
Do you think your worrying would be less if you were sleeping well?
I mean... you just asked me that. I still don't know. I haven't had a good night's sleep in a really long time, so... I can't really say if it would make a difference.
Do you think your worrying would stop if you fell asleep quickly and slept through the night?
I... I don't know how else to answer that. You keep asking me the same thing, but... I just don't know. I really don't have a different answer for you.
Is there one main thing that you worry about most of the time

No, not really one thing. It's... it's a lot of things. Most days it just kind of jumps around. Like, I'll be worried about hitting our launch numbers at work, and then I'm suddenly thinking about whether someone on my team is going to quit. And then it's the mortgage, or... or a client renewal. It just feels like... like any small delay could turn into a huge disaster. So, no, it's not just one main thing.
Do you think your worrying would decrease if you were able to fall asleep and stay asleep through the night
I... we've talked about this a few times now. I don't know what else to tell you. I just... I don't know if it would help.
Is your worrying usually about a specific area of your life or is it more general, covering many different things?
I... I think I just said this. It's... it's a lot of things. Work, the team, the house... it just moves around. It's not just one thing.
